doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Clip-on microphones and sound engineers
summary: Sam dislikes clip-on mics and clashes with sound people.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: I mentioned, before we started we were talking about playing into microphones, clip on microphones and all that. How do you feel about that?

I don’t like clip on microphones too much. They just don’t allow you to be as expressive. Because if you have like a mic you can pull back from it and control your volume and where if you’re clipped on you can do that but you have to turn your stuff up and down. But I don’t know, that’s why I have all these scratches here because I’m always like — and I get yelled at a lot by it too, because they’ll be too loud and the soundman has to turn me down and then I can’t hear myself so I go even farther into the microphone and it feeds back. But that’s the battle over my saxophone and microphones.
Do you ever get into verbal arguments with sound people?

Oh yeah. They get mad. They definitely, after a while, you don’t piss off the sound guy or the monitor guy especially, if there is one. Because he could make or break your sound easily. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
Especially if you’re a warm-up act. I know it used to happen to us. Why should they make you sound good? And it’s not like you have enough money to throw them a few bucks either, you know?
I know. Why give them a hard time. Actually it doesn’t work either.
